pull.title: KAFKA-21230: Pause task executors on byte limit
pull.body:
#23728 pauses processing and punctuation while the uncommitted state
store bytes of a StreamThread exceed `statestore.uncommitted.max.bytes`.
That pause is in `runOnceWithoutProcessingThreads`. When processing
threads are enabled, task executors process records and run punctuators
independently of the StreamThread loop, so the pause does not stop them.
If a commit is skipped during a rebalance, or fails, the executors
continue to write to the state stores. The uncommitted bytes then
increase without bound, and the native memory of the transaction buffers
increases with them.

`StreamThread#maybePauseProcessingForUncommittedBytes()` now also sets
the pause on the processing threads, through the new
`TaskManager#setProcessingThreadsPaused`. `runOnceWithProcessingThreads`
calls it after `maybeCommit`. The scheduling `TaskManager` gains
`setProcessingPaused` and `processingPaused`.

`DefaultTaskManager` keeps the flag in a volatile field for each
StreamThread. It does not use `TaskExecutionMetadata`, because all
StreamThreads share that object. While the flag is set, `canProgress`
returns false, so `assignNextTask` assigns no task and
`awaitProcessableTasks` blocks. When processing resumes,
`DefaultTaskManager` signals the executors. While paused,
`DefaultTaskExecutor` does not process or punctuate its current task.
The task makes no progress, so the executor releases it through the
existing path for such tasks.

`GlobalStreamThread` does not need this change. One thread writes,
checks and flushes synchronously, and no condition skips the flush.

Both tests in `UncommittedBytesLimitIntegrationTest` now also run with
processing threads enabled.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

Reviewers: Bill Bejeck <bbejeck@apache.org>

review_comments.body: With the Streams group protocol, a status-only heartbeat such as `ASSIGNMENT_DELAYED` can mark the group not ready while retaining active tasks. The early return at line 1427 then bypasses both commits and this pause check, so executors can keep processing and punctuating without the byte limit taking effect. Call `maybePauseProcessingForUncommittedBytes()` before that early return too, and add a processing-thread test for a ready-to-not-ready transition with retained tasks.

nit: `canPunctuateTask` isn't stubbed here, so the mock returns false and the punctuate branch is never entered, paused or not. That means the `never().maybePunctuateStreamTime()` / `never().maybePunctuateSystemTime()` checks pass even if the `!processingPaused` check on punctuation is removed.
nit:  No test covers this forwarding. `StreamThreadTest` mocks `TaskManager`, so if this call became a no-op, every test would still pass

commit.message:
KAFKA-21230: Pause processing threads on uncommitted bytes

When processing threads are enabled, task executors process records
and run punctuators independently of the StreamThread loop. Thus the
pause in runOnceWithoutProcessingThreads does not stop them. If a
commit is skipped during a rebalance, or fails, the executors continue
to write to the state stores, and the uncommitted bytes continue to
increase without bound.

StreamThread#maybePauseProcessingForUncommittedBytes() now also sets
the pause on the processing threads, through the new
TaskManager#setProcessingThreadsPaused. runOnceWithProcessingThreads
calls it after maybeCommit. The scheduling TaskManager gains
setProcessingPaused and processingPaused. DefaultTaskManager keeps the
flag in a volatile field for each StreamThread. It does not use
TaskExecutionMetadata, because all StreamThreads share that object.
While the flag is set, canProgress returns false, so assignNextTask
assigns no task and awaitProcessableTasks blocks. When processing
resumes, DefaultTaskManager signals the executors. While paused,
DefaultTaskExecutor does not process or punctuate its current task.
The task makes no progress, so the executor releases it through the
existing path for tasks that make no progress.

GlobalStreamThread does not need this change. One thread writes,
checks and flushes synchronously, and no condition skips the flush.

Both tests in UncommittedBytesLimitIntegrationTest now also run with
processing threads enabled.

commit.message:
KAFKA-21230: Pause processing threads when group not ready

When processing threads are enabled and the Streams group becomes not
ready, runOnceWithProcessingThreads returns early. Thus it does not
call maybePauseProcessingForUncommittedBytes(). But the thread keeps
its tasks, and the task executors continue to process them. Nothing
commits, so the uncommitted bytes can increase without a limit.

runOnceWithProcessingThreads now calls
maybePauseProcessingForUncommittedBytes() before the early return. The
byte limit then applies while the group is not ready.

A new StreamThreadTest test,
shouldPauseProcessingThreadsWhileUncommittedBytesExceedLimitAndStreamsGroupNotReady,
covers the change from a ready group to a group that is not ready.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit.message:
KAFKA-21230: Make paused unassign test fail without pause check

shouldUnassignTaskWhileProcessingPaused verifies that the executor
does not process or punctuate the task while processing is paused. But
the mocked task was not processable and could not punctuate. Thus the
never() checks passed even when the pause check was removed.

The test now stubs task.isProcessable and canPunctuateTask to return
true. If the pause check is removed, the executor processes and
punctuates the task, and the test fails.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit.message:
KAFKA-21230: Test forwarding of processing threads pause

No test covered how TaskManager#setProcessingThreadsPaused forwards
the pause to the scheduling TaskManager, because StreamThreadTest
mocks TaskManager.

shouldForwardProcessingThreadsPausedToSchedulingTaskManager verifies
that the flag goes to the scheduling TaskManager.
shouldNotForwardProcessingThreadsPausedWithoutProcessingThreads
verifies that the call does nothing when processing threads are not
enabled.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
